nl -ba docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md | sed -n '1,340p'"","aggregated_output":"     1	# Durable managed host runs, reviewer receipts, and usage diagnostics
     2	
     3	Proofbound launches Codex and Claude as managed cross-provider CLI processes.
     4	`lattice host_run` submits those processes to a durable
     5	`ManagedHostRun`: the detached worker, not the caller shell, owns the provider
     6	until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
     7	return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.
     8	
     9	The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not
    10	the execution owner and disabling them does not disable shared provider-process
    11	admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions
    12	that never used the managed boundary.
    13	
    14	## Why this exists
    15	
    16	A 2026-07-10 token-burn audit found the usage ledger only ever saw a handful of
    17	probe rows: host-side reviewer launches, quorum cross-host reviews, and long
    18	desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
    19	`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive
    20	terminal receipt. The runtime persists under the primary worktree at
    21	`.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`, so Story worktree cleanup cannot erase an
    22	active run or its receipt; secrets and prompt bytes are 0600
    23	one-shot inputs removed when the worker claims them. Interactive desktop and
    24	native-subagent lifecycles remain outside this boundary and are covered only by
    25	their host or by read-only retrospective diagnostics.
    26	
    27	Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the
    28	workflow, never satisfy REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority evidence, and never advance a
    29	phase.
    30	
    31	## `host_run`
    32	
    33	```
    34	lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
    35	  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
    36	  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
    37	  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
    38	  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
    39	  [--json]
    40	```
    41	
    42	`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
    43	`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
    44	run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:
    45	
    46	```bash
    47	lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
    48	lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
    49	```
    50	
    51	`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
    52	inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
    53	only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
    54	receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
    55	never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
    56	absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
    57	touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
    58	cleanup made replacement safe.
    59	
    60	The host subprocess executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
    61	target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
    62	the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
    63	never diverge from where the ledger says it ran.
    64	
    65	Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
    66	caller as it arrives, up to the per-run 8 MiB retention ceiling. The foreground
    67	projection is explicitly bounded: once the ceiling is reached, `--json` reports
    68	`truncated=true` on the `lattice.host_run.v1` result and text mode writes
    69	`truncated=true` to stderr; neither promises the omitted tail.
    70	`host_run_status --json` exposes the same flag as `output.truncated`. Worker
    71	heartbeat and `lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
    72	the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
    73	only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
    74	is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
    75	is written to stderr, for example:
    76	
    77	```
    78	usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
    79	```
    80	
    81	Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
    82	usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
    83	capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
    84	flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
    85	poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
    86	happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
    87	retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
    88	usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
    89	rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
    90	valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
    91	later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
    92	(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
    93	perfectly good final usage event).
    94	
    95	### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)
    96	
    97	| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
    98	|---|---|---|---|
    99	| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
   100	| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |
   101	
   102	In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
   103	delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
   104	result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the JSON result reports
   105	`truncated=true` and does not promise the omitted tail; the JSON `stdout` field
   106	carries only the bounded usage-parse tail, not an unbounded or complete
   107	transcript.
   108	
   109	If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
   110	but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
   111	`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
   112	`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
   113	downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
   114	delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
   115	event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
   116	stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
   117	stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
   118	contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
   119	once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
   120	skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
   121	passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
   122	outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
   123	serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
   124	by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
   125	command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
   126	from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
   127	fires while a listener is attached. If the drain cap wins, one shared guard stays
   128	per physical stream until each pending write settles; its release is deferred
   129	through the next event-loop turn because Node `Writable` can invoke the write
   130	callback before emitting the same failed write's `EPIPE` event. This contains the real
   131	callback-then-error ordering without retaining one listener per foreground run.
   132	
   133	Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
   134	runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
   135	forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
   136	non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
   137	`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.
   138	
   139	### Reviewer launch
   140	
   141	Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
   142	when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
   143	registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
   144	lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
   145	identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
   146	registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
   147	in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
   148	attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
   149	process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.
   150	
   151	An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
   152	`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
   153	review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
   154	the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
   155	direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
   156	below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
   157	capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
   158	registered broker set.
   159	
   160	`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers` is an object containing a `brokers` array. Each
   161	registration has all four required fields: `brokerId` (the unique trusted broker
   162	name), `adapterId` (the adapter identity the attestation claims), `host` (exactly
   163	`"codex"` or `"claude"`), and `publicKey` (the broker's Ed25519 public key).
   164	For example:
   165	
   166	```json
   167	{
   168	  "nativeReviewInvocation": {
   169	    "brokers": [{
   170	      "brokerId": "desktop-codex-review-broker",
   171	      "adapterId": "desktop-codex-adapter-v1",
   172	      "host": "codex",
   173	      "publicKey": "<Ed25519 public key>"
   174	    }]
   175	  }
   176	}
   177	```
   178	
   179	The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
   180	ledger is replay protection, not a same-UID security boundary. Likewise process
   181	ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
   182	view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
   183	Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
   184	matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
   185	instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.
   186	
   187	Reviewer Prompt 不应由调用方手工拼接或假定某个 rollout mode。先由
   188	`review_run_start` 按当前 Story、lane 和 `promptEnvelope.roles` 的逐角色 flag
   189	选择可信正文与 full/incremental context，再让 `host_run --managedReview`
   190	按 `reviewRunId` 重新取得并校验这份内容。当前可独立启用 `lattice-review-concept`、
   191	`lattice-review-quality`、`lattice-review-test-coverage`、
   192	`lattice-review-behavior`、`lattice-review-docs`；未启用角色保持
   193	`legacy-full-context`，retired channel 不可进入该 rollout。
   194	
   195	ReviewRun 摘要会记录 rollout mode、role-body/context/assembled digest、selection
   196	reason 和预算判定。reviewer 如发现增量材料不足，必须通过既有 escalation
   197	reason 请求 full context；feature flag 本身不会授予 incremental eligibility，
   198	也不会改变 pass/finding 的签名与 freshness 门禁。在途 legacy pass 仍只按其
   199	原始 ReviewRun/round/Envelope 解释，不能因后来切换 flag 被重新绑定。
   200	
   201	```bash
   202	# 1. Controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
   203	lattice review_run_start '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","agent":"lattice-review-quality"}'
   204	
   205	# 2. Submit the exact provider reviewer; raw `bash + codex exec` is unmanaged.
   206	lattice host_run '{"host":"codex","storyId":"B-xxxx","agentType":"lattice-review-quality","reviewRunId":"B-xxxx:RR-001","lane":"lattice-review-quality","managedReview":true,"detach":true,"json":true}'
   207	
   208	# 3. Repeat this bounded status call. Silence does not cause replacement.
   209	lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":<generation>,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
   210	
   211	# 4. Import only after completed + replacementSafe=true + reaped=true + residualProcessGroup=false.
   212	lattice managed_review_evidence_import '{"runId":"<runId>","receiptId":"<receiptId>"}'
   213	```
   214	
   215	Inside the provider process, the managed prompt forbids `review_run_start`,
   216	`review_pass_set` and `finding_add`. Its final assistant result must be exactly
   217	one bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope containing
   218	pass-or-findings plus truthful read evidence. This protocol overrides the generic
   219	reviewer role template's normal `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` closing rules.
   220	After a successful provider exit,
   221	the managed adapter selects only Codex's terminal `item.completed`
   222	`agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs, arbitrary streamed
   223	stdout and controller fields are ignored. The worker validates the sealed
   224	story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal.
   225	Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized envelopes fail the run closed. The
   226	`pass` form requires a non-empty note and no findings (an empty findings array is
   227	equivalent to absence). The `findings` form requires at least one fully valid
   228	finding and may carry a non-empty explanatory note. Both the canonical final
   229	envelope and the older compatibility proposal ingress accept that diagnostic
   230	note, then discard it before the immutable evidence proposal is written, so it
   231	can never become a formal finding or evidence field. Whitespace-only notes,
   232	missing findings, malformed envelopes, and oversized provider final results
   233	fail closed. The older
   234	descriptor-authorized `managed_review_proposal_set` command remains a
   235	compatibility path, not the formal happy path; its private signing key is never
   236	placed in the prompt, argv, provider environment, or durable run artifact.
   237	Raw same-UID CLI calls, copied environment variables, stale PGIDs,
   238	terminal/reaped runs, and ambiguous/multiple run candidates fail closed.
   239	Successful terminal creation seals the proposal and journal. That state alone
   240	is not importable: the receipt must also prove `replacementSafe=true`,
   241	`processCleanup.reaped=true`, and
   242	`processCleanup.residualProcessGroup=false`. The importer accepts only
   243	`runId + receiptId`, exposes no verdict override, and preserves the provider
   244	lane/ReviewRun/provenance. Both import time and the REVIEW gate revalidate the
   245	same shared Proof Admissibility contract. Raw CLI stdout,
   246	usage rows and time-window correlations cannot satisfy this evidence class.
   247	
   248	For a managed Claude reviewer, the worker materializes the authoritative prompt
   249	as a mode-`0600` one-shot file below the provider's exact working directory at
   250	`.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/`; Claude's workspace sandbox can therefore
   251	read it without exposing prompt text in argv. Because a detached reviewer has no
   252	interactive terminal on which to approve required inspection and Lattice CLI
   253	commands, only the signed `managed_reviewer` launch profile adds Claude's
   254	`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. That same profile supplies a bounded,
   255	non-secret `--json-schema` which fixes the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun
   256	tuple and proposal vocabulary. The schema is an unavoidable CLI argument, but
   257	contains neither prompt/capability bytes nor a controller-authored conclusion.
   258	The adapter consumes only a `type=result` event with `subtype=success` and a
   259	present provider-validated `structured_output`. Every other Claude result
   260	event is ignored, including error/non-success envelopes and success events
   261	without `structured_output`. Ordinary prose, Markdown-fenced JSON, and
   262	`event.result` are never proposal inputs. Ordinary Claude `host_run` keeps its
   263	configured permission policy and has no JSON schema, while Codex keeps stdin
   264	transport. The private leaf is removed when the provider settles. Missing,
   265	prose-only, malformed, multiple, or oversized proposal envelopes still fail
   266	closed.
   267	
   268	`host_run_worker` is an internal continuation command. It remains dispatchable
   269	by the detached launcher but is omitted from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
   270	operators use `host_run`, `host_run_status`, and `host_run_cancel`.
   271	
   272	### Ordinary/quorum managed runs
   273	
   274	```
   275	# Codex host
   276	lattice host_run --host codex --storyId B-xxxx --agentType quorum-reviewer \
   277	  --reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-002 --lane lattice-review-quality \
   278	  --promptFile quorum-prompt.txt
   279	
   280	# Claude host
   281	lattice host_run --host claude --storyId B-xxxx --agentType quorum-reviewer \
   282	  --reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-002 --lane lattice-review-quality \
   283	  --promptFile quorum-prompt.txt
   284	
   285	```
   286	
   287	The current agy print CLI accepts prompt bytes only as a plaintext argv value.
   288	It is therefore not a managed `host_run` host and is absent from that command's
   289	public schema. Antigravity/agy remains available only on diagnostic host-runtime
   290	surfaces; a future managed adapter would require stdin or protected prompt-file
   291	transport before it could be added as a new execution capability.
   292	
   293	## Binding conventions
   294	
   295	Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:
   296	
   297	| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |
   298	|---|---|---|
   299	| `--storyId` | `storyId` | Canonical Story id. Omit for an adhoc run. |
   300	| `--agentType` | `agentType` | e.g. `reviewer`, `autopilot-repair`, `host-readiness-probe`. Required. |
   301	| `--phase` | `phase` | When omitted and `--storyId` is set, the phase resolves from the **configured story store** at call time (honoring a project's `storyDir`); an explicit `--phase` is used as-is and the store is never read. |
   302	| `--reviewRunId` | `threadId` | e.g. `B-xxxx:RR-001`. Joins rows against `review-runs.json`. |
   303	| `--lane` | `subagentId` | e.g. `lattice-review-quality`. |
   304	
   305	`--reviewRunId` must start with `<storyId>:` when `--storyId` is given, so a
   306	ledger row can never silently mis-join across stories — a mismatch is refused
   307	before any host is spawned. Omitting `--reviewRunId` / `--lane` leaves
   308	`threadId` / `subagentId` null (no empty-string pollution).
   309	
   310	When `--storyId` is given **without** `--phase`, the phase is resolved through the
   311	configured story store; a story unknown to that store is refused pre-spawn. When
   312	`--phase` is supplied the store is never consulted, so `--phase` works with or
   313	without `--storyId` even in a project whose story metadata lives under a
   314	custom `storyDir`.
   315	
   316	## Per-host usage semantics
   317	
   318	Provider truth is preferred over estimates; an absence is recorded as an explicit
   319	`source=unavailable`, never a fabricated zero.
   320	
   321	- **codex** — parses the terminal `turn.completed` usage event from
   322	  `codex exec --json` and maps it to `{ input: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens,
   323	  cacheRead: cached_input_tokens, cacheCreation: null, output: output_tokens }`.
   324	  The `input` field is the **uncached remainder** (codex `input_tokens` includes
   325	  cached input); the original payload (including `reasoning_output_tokens`) is
   326	  digested raw.
   327	- **claude** — parses the stream-json `result` envelope usage via
   328	  `parseClaudeCliOutput` (the four-field Anthropic usage plus the served model).
   329	
   330	A parse miss (no `turn.completed` event, no `result` usage) records an
   331	`unavailable` final with a reason rather than inventing counts.
   332	
   333	同样的诚实口径适用于 reviewer A/B：缺少 exact per-role historical envelope、
   334	reviewer output、adjudication bytes 或 provider receipt 时结果是
   335	`INCONCLUSIVE`，不是“0 token”或已证明的节省。B-235e 的独立 replay campaign
   336	因此不声称达到计划中的 50% incremental / 40% assembled 降幅。
   337	
   338	The one-line usage summary reflects the **actual append outcome**, not merely
   339	that the provider envelope parsed. When the ledger append itself fails (a corrupt
   340	ledger, or a lock-wait timeout that skips the write), the summary reports a
   341	skipped state (`recorded: none`, reason `ledger_append_failed(...)`) and the
   342	stderr line reads `usage: ledger_append_failed(...)` — it never claims
   343	`usage recorded` for a row that never landed. This applies to both managed hosts;
   344	the provider is still surfaced for attribution, but token counts stay null. A
   345	provider record that BUILT fine but whose append failed is reported as an
   346	append failure keyed on the parsed usage — it is **never degraded to
   347	`source=unavailable`** (which would falsely read as "the provider reported
   348	nothing"), and no second `unavailable` final is attempted for it.
   349	
   350	The same honesty gate covers the **blocked rows**: a cap refusal claims
   351	`recorded: blocked` (and, for a concurrency refusal, surfaces the blocked row's
   352	`recordId`) only when the blocked row **actually appended**. When that append is
   353	swallowed too, the refusal itself is unchanged — still fail-closed, no spawn,
   354	non-zero exit — but the summary reports `recorded: none` with `recordId: null`
   355	and a composed reason that keeps the refusal visible, e.g.
   356	`hard_budget_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)` or
   357	`concurrency_cap_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)`. A recordId is never
   358	minted for a blocked row that never persisted.
   359	
   360	## Provider execution surfaces
   361	
   362	Every production provider spawn site carries a `ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus`
   363	and is enumerated by `provider-execution-inventory-contract`, which fails if a
   364	new spawn path appears unclassified:
   365	
   366	- `managed` — runs through ManagedHostRun (durable run identity, supervised
   367	  process group, absolute deadline, one terminal receipt).
   368	- `admission_only` — not managed-executed, but still routed through the shared
   369	  admission boundary, so the concurrency cap below applies.
   370	- `adapter_only` — a low-level adapter whose caller owns admission.
   371	- `readiness_probe` — version/readiness checks only; never review evidence.
   372	- `legacy_unmanaged` — neither managed nor admission-routed. Reserved and
   373	  **currently empty by contract**: the inventory test asserts no surface uses
   374	  it, so introducing one is a deliberate, reviewable act.
   375	
   376	There is no `admission_managed` status — admission and managed execution are
   377	independent properties, spelled `admission_only` and `managed`.
   378	
   379	See `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` for
   380	the decision record.
   381	
   382	## Caps (fail-closed, before spawn)
   383	
   384	With the usage ledger enabled, both caps run at the choke point BEFORE a host
   385	is spawned, and each refusal attempts to record a
   386	`decision.kind=blocked` ledger row (diagnostics-honest; an append failure is
   387	reported as `recorded: none`). With `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0`, budget enforcement
   388	and every ledger row are disabled; the provider-process capacity admission
   389	still runs before every spawn and refuses fail-closed without claiming a
   390	blocked row was persisted.
   391	
   392	- **Per-dispatch hard budget** — reuses the existing `LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS`
   393	  preflight guard per call. An over-budget preflight estimate refuses with
   394	  `reasonCode hard_budget_exceeded` before spawning.
   395	- **Provider-process concurrency** — a shared slot registry under
   396	  `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/`
   397	  holds **fixed numbered slots** `slot-0.json` .. `slot-(cap-1).json`, one per
   398	  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
   399	  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
   400	  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.
   401	  The lock makes the live-count check, stale reclaim, cap-lowering check and
   402	  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
   403	  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index
   404	  under `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default **4**; unset / invalid /
   405	  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
   406	  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
   407	  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
   408	  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
   409	  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
   410	  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimed at any age; a slot
   411	  whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between creating
   412	  the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime exceeds the
   413	  `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default **6h**); a slot
   414	  with a **live** recorded pid is **never reclaimed by age** — a long host run
   415	  keeps its admission and waiters refuse at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
   416	  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
   417	  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
   418	  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
   419	  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
   420	  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
   421	  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
   422	  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
   423	  counts every live high-index slot and refuses new starts until the total live
   424	  count drops below the new cap.
   425	
   426	Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the managed
   427	host that was asked to run (`openai` for codex or `anthropic` for claude), never
   428	a hard-coded default.
   429	
   430	The autopilot Claude repair launch (`lattice autopilot execute
   431	--allowClaudeRepair`) passes the **same pre-spawn admission** in both ledger
   432	modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the
   433	diagnostic blocked row. With the ledger OFF there are no usage rows or budget
   434	guard, but capacity admission remains mandatory and the slot is still released
   435	after the run.
   436	
   437	The `cross_host_review` Codex leaf runs through ManagedHostRun and the same
   438	provider admission (provider `openai`). It supports detach/resume by exact
   439	`managedRunId`, never spawns a replacement on resume, and binds the terminal
   440	`receiptId` into host-B verdict provenance. Budget/cap/provider failures still
   441	produce an honest blocked/error decision; raw stdout is never gate evidence.
   442	
   443	Concurrent runs' ledger appends are serialized by a cross-process lock at the
   444	writer choke point (an atomic `llm-usage.jsonl.lock/` directory with a bounded
   445	wait), so parallel host runs can never interleave appends and break the ledger
   446	hash chain — a writer that cannot acquire the lock in time skips its append
   447	(an honest under-count) rather than corrupting the chain. Lock reclaim is
   448	ownership-aware: the acquirer records `owner.json` (holder pid + a unique
   449	release token) inside the lock dir, and a held lock is reclaimed only when
   450	that pid is dead, or — for an ownerless/corrupt lock, i.e. the holder crashed
   451	between creating the dir and recording ownership — when the dir mtime exceeds
   452	the `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_MS` orphan backstop. A live holder is
   453	never reclaimed no matter how long it holds the lock (slow filesystem, GC
   454	pause, suspension); release removes the lock only while `owner.json` still
   455	carries the releaser's own token.
   456	
   457	There is **no queuing** in this story: over the cap means refuse, not wait.
   458	
   459	Set `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0` to disable usage preflight/budget/final rows. It
   460	does **not** disable ManagedHostRun ownership or provider-process admission.
     1	# Managed cross-provider CLI execution
     2	
     3	Status: Adopted
     4	Story: B-137a
     5	Date: 2026-08-14
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	When a Claude host started Codex (or a Codex host started Claude) with raw shell
    10	execution, the caller owned the child process implicitly. A caller watchdog,
    11	terminal disconnect, or ten-minute foreground boundary could end observation
    12	without proving that the provider had failed. Treating that loss of observation
    13	as failure caused duplicate reviewer launches; treating `running` forever as
    14	proof of health caused unbounded waits. Output silence alone answers neither
    15	question.
    16	
    17	Proofbound is host-neutral. Native Codex/Claude subagent lifecycle APIs are not
    18	portable and therefore are not the execution contract. This decision covers
    19	only Proofbound-owned cross-provider CLI processes.
    20	
    21	## Decision
    22	
    23	Proofbound owns every public `host_run` and every formal cross-provider CLI
    24	reviewer launch through a durable `ManagedHostRun`. General provider workloads
    25	such as planned steps and autopilot repair keep their existing bounded adapters
    26	but share the mandatory provider-process admission registry; they do not claim
    27	durable reviewer ownership or reviewer evidence. The caller submits and
    28	observes; a detached worker owns the managed provider process until an exclusive
    29	terminal record exists.
    30	
    31	The public surface is:
    32	
    33	- `host_run`: submit, optionally attach in foreground, or return after claim
    34	  with `--detach`;
    35	- `host_run_status`: read or long-poll one run for at most 30 seconds;
    36	- `host_run_cancel`: idempotently request cancellation;
    37	- `host_run_worker`: private runtime continuation, dispatchable internally but
    38	  hidden from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
    39	- `managed_review_proposal_set`: compatibility-only provider callback for older
    40	  adapters, not the formal managed happy path;
    41	- `managed_review_evidence_import`: verdict-free exact-receipt importer.
    42	
    43	`cross_host_review` remains the policy/profile owner for paired host verdicts,
    44	but its Codex leaf executes inside ManagedHostRun and exposes the managed run
    45	and receipt in host-B provenance.
    46	
    47	## State and liveness contract
    48	
    49	The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
    50	`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
    51	status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
    52	
    53	Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
    54	
    55	- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
    56	  snapshot;
    57	- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
    58	  arrives.
    59	
    60	Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
    61	and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
    62	observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
    63	a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
    64	however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
    65	absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
    66	`timed_out` terminal state.
    67	
    68	Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
    69	hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
    70	reap and residual probing. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove
    71	there is no residual process group. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity remains
    72	`replacementSafe=false`; it is not guessed away.
    73	
    74	## Persistence and process ownership
    75	
    76	Each run has a 0700 directory at
    77	`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
    78	primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
    79	DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
    80	bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
    81	capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
    82	Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
    83	the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
    84	runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
    85	
    86	On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
    87	prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`). Claude receives a 0600
    88	one-shot prompt file below the exact provider cwd's ignored
    89	`.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/` tree, because Claude's workspace sandbox
    90	rejects an otherwise protected OS-temp prompt outside that cwd. Prompt text never
    91	enters argv and the private leaf is removed after settlement. A detached formal
    92	Claude reviewer has no approval terminal, so only the signed `managed_reviewer`
    93	profile launches it with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; ordinary Claude
    94	host runs retain their configured policy, and the strict final proposal/parser
    95	boundary is unchanged. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only
    96	in argv, so managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy
    97	exposes a stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms
    98	likewise refuse before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup
    99	is equivalent.
   100	
   101	## Shared provider admission
   102	
   103	Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
   104	of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
   105	token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
   106	Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
   107	not process admission.
   108	
   109	A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
   110	reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
   111	checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
   112	already been reclaimed and reassigned.
   113	
   114	Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
   115	admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
   116	review evidence.
   117	
   118	### Provider execution surface classification
   119	
   120	Every production provider spawn site is classified by
   121	`ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus` (`packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts`),
   122	and `packages/main/src/tasks/provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts` fails if a
   123	new spawn path appears without one:
   124	
   125	| Status | Meaning |
   126	|---|---|
   127	| `managed` | Executes through ManagedHostRun: durable run identity, supervised process group, absolute deadline, exactly one terminal receipt. |
   128	| `admission_only` | Not managed-executed, but routed through the shared provider admission boundary, so the concurrency cap and slot accounting still apply. |
   129	| `adapter_only` | A low-level adapter module whose *caller* owns admission; the adapter itself makes no gate claim. |
   130	| `readiness_probe` | Version/readiness probing only. Never becomes review evidence. |
   131	| `legacy_unmanaged` | A provider spawn that is neither managed nor admission-routed. **Reserved, and currently empty by contract.** |
   132	
   133	`admission_managed` is not a status value: admission and managed execution are
   134	two separate properties, expressed by `admission_only` (admission without
   135	managed execution) and `managed` (both).
   136	
   137	The `legacy_unmanaged` bucket exists so an unmanaged spawn path must be declared
   138	rather than pass silently. It is asserted empty — `provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts`
   139	requires that no surface carries it — so adding one is a deliberate, reviewable
   140	act that fails the contract until justified. It is not a claim that unmanaged
   141	execution is impossible, only that none is currently admitted.
   142	
   143	## Formal managed reviewer evidence
   144	
   145	Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
   146	ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:
   147	
   148	1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
   149	2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
   150	   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
   151	   bindings.
   152	3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
   153	   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
   154	   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
   155	   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. This
   156	   protocol overrides the generic reviewer role
   157	   template's direct pass/finding closing instructions: the provider returns the
   158	   envelope only, and the managed adapter is the sole proposal writer.
   159	   After a successful provider exit, the owning adapter selects only Codex's terminal
   160	   `item.completed` `agent_message` or Claude's successful terminal
   161	   provider-validated `structured_output` (`type=result`, `subtype=success`,
   162	   field present). Claude non-success result events, success events without
   163	   `structured_output`, and `event.result` are ignored. Claude's signed
   164	   managed-review launch supplies a bounded non-secret `--json-schema` bound
   165	   to the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple. Tool logs, arbitrary
   166	   stdout, Claude prose or fenced JSON, and controller fields are never
   167	   proposal inputs. The worker
   168	   validates the same tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal.
   169	   Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final envelopes fail the managed
   170	   run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
   171	   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
   172	4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result, live-output and
   173	   event-journal digests plus cleanup facts.
   174	5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
   175	   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes. Import still
   176	   fails closed unless the completed receipt proves `replacementSafe=true`,
   177	   `processCleanup.reaped=true`, and
   178	   `processCleanup.residualProcessGroup=false`.
   179	6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
   180	   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
   181	7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
   182	   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
   183	   journal, prompt and material tuple.
   184	
   185	Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
   186	proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
   187	cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
   188	environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
   189	ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.
   190	
   191	The worker's reserved durable cancellation reason
   192	`absolute_deadline_exceeded` always reconciles to a `timed_out` terminal with
   193	that exact reason, even if the next observation occurs through the cancellation
   194	branch. Human/operator cancellation remains `cancelled`; both paths retain the
   195	same cleanup and replacement-safety proof.
   196	
   197	The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
   198	signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
   199	host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
   200	binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
   201	adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public
   202	key and nonce-consumption record, but exposes no issuer command and stores no
   203	broker private key. `dispatch`, `review_run_start`, inherited environment values
   204	and raw provider CLIs cannot mint this authority. The host adapter must inject
   205	the signed attestation over a dedicated descriptor for the exact CLI process;
   206	without that integration, native direct evidence is advisory-only and formal
   207	review must use the managed path.
   208

    15	## 1. Decision
    16	
    17	Proofbound will replace default broad specification reads with a hybrid retrieval pipeline:
    18	
    19	1. the CLI derives deterministic search terms from structured Story facts;
    20	2. Codex CLI and Claude Code CLI independently propose semantic expansions;
    21	3. no third proposer is attempted unless a future provider gains a protected managed transport;
    22	4. the CLI performs bounded local filename, heading, and content search;
    23	5. a deterministic ranker produces an auditable `candidateSpecSet`;
    24	6. reviewers read candidate documents in full and title-triage the rest;
    25	7. ambiguity, high-risk changes, or weak recall triggers an explicitly recorded broader scan.
    26	
    27	Model output is advisory routing input. It is never gate evidence. Signed scope-check, reviewer-pass, finding, validation, and delivery artifacts remain the only lifecycle evidence.

    29	## 2. Problem
    30	
    31	B-f97c removed the immediate failure mode where every `story_review` prompt embedded the complete requirements corpus. That stopgap prevents routine prompt size from scaling with corpus size, but it intentionally does not solve relevant-document discovery.

    33	The next problem is recall under a bounded read budget:
    34	
    35	- deterministic keywords may miss historical synonyms;
    36	- one model may reproduce the Story's current wording and miss legacy vocabulary;

    38	- `relatedDocs` is curated by the owner and cannot be the sole truth source;
    39	- a top-N cap without ambiguity handling can hide a relevant document near the cutoff;
    40	- reviewer prose cannot prove which files were actually read.

   121	## 7. Deterministic keyword contract
   122	
   123	The CLI MUST derive seeds before launching any host. Sources, in priority order:
   124	
   125	1. explicit `relatedDocs` paths and anchors;
   126	2. Story title, description, keywords, risk signals, and acceptance wording;
   127	3. checklist titles, `userSees`, and `excludes`;
   128	4. understanding touchpoints and declared files;
   129	5. changed paths, exported symbols, command names, config keys, artifact names, and process-fact names;
   130	6. exact identifiers extracted from backticks, flags, JSON keys, environment variables, and error codes;
   131	7. bounded memory/playbook hits, labeled advisory and non-authoritative.
   132	
   133	Each seed records:
   134	
   135	```ts
   136	interface DeterministicKeywordSeed {
   137	  term: string;
   138	  normalizedTerm: string;
   139	  sourceType: 'relatedDoc' | 'story' | 'checklist' | 'touchpoint' |
   140	    'changedFile' | 'symbol' | 'command' | 'configKey' | 'artifact' |
   141	    'processFact' | 'memoryAdvisory';
   142	  sourceRef: string;
   143	  weight: number;
   144	}
   145	```
   146	
   147	Normalization MUST preserve exact identifiers alongside lowercase lexical forms. Hyphen, underscore, slash, camelCase, and acronym variants may be added, but the original token cannot be discarded.

   149	## 8. Host keyword proposal contract
   150	
   151	### 8.1 Default host policy
   152	
   153	- Primary proposers: Codex CLI and Claude Code CLI.
   154	- No supplemental proposer is currently supported. Primary failure or disagreement
   155	  is recorded and deterministic local routing continues without an unlaunchable host.
   156	- No host proposal can expand lifecycle authority or satisfy a gate.
   157	
   158	### 8.2 Fresh-context input
   159	
   160	The CLI first applies one pre-egress sanitizer to every field and artifact that could enter a host prompt. There is no alternate adapter path around this boundary. The sanitizer:
   161	
   162	- transmits identifier, command, configuration, and environment-variable names, never detected values;
   163	- redacts secret-like values in Story/checklist prose, backticks, error payloads, paths, titles, symbols, seeds, and memory-derived text;
   164	- hashes or omits sensitive provenance and `sourceRef` values while retaining a local-only mapping for audit;
   165	- rejects and records unsafe host inputs or outputs instead of trying to repair them;
   166	- treats uncertain classification as sensitive and skips the host call, continuing with deterministic local routing;
   167	- persists only the sanitized request digest and sanitized proposal artifact.
   168	
   169	After sanitization, each host receives only:
   170	
   171	- Story ID, title, description, keywords, and risk signals;
   172	- checklist title, `userSees`, `excludes`, and related-doc paths;
   173	- deterministic seed list with provenance;
   174	- changed files/symbols when available;
   175	- complete decisions filename/title index, without document bodies;
   176	- proposal budget and output schema.
   177	
   178	The host does not receive the entire requirements corpus, the owner's full conversation, raw secret-bearing metadata, or the local-only provenance map.

   550	## 20. Validation matrix
   551	
   552	| Scenario | Expected result |
   553	|---|---|
   554	| Exact related doc | rank 1 with explicit-path reason |
   555	| Sparse matches | retain deterministic seeds, record low coverage, and escalate when the source-class floor is not met |
   556	| Noisy/excessive matches | deduplicate and rank within configured result budgets; truncation that can change the cutoff escalates |
   557	| Zero-candidate result | record the empty result and ambiguity reason, then use bounded escalation; never silently inject or fully scan the corpus |
   558	| Legacy synonym proposed by one host | local hit enters candidates with host provenance |
   559	| Both hosts miss exact config key | deterministic seed still retrieves document |
   560	| Codex/Claude disagree at cutoff | ambiguity escalation |
   561	| `agy` (never attempted; diagnostic-only) | primary pair continues; agy availability is recorded for diagnostics but agy is never launched — see §1/§8.1/§8.2/§22 |
   562	| Both primary hosts unavailable | deterministic path continues; no automatic full scan |
   563	| Memory no-hit | bounded search continues |
   564	| High-risk gate change | recorded broad-scan escalation |
   565	| Irrelevant 5 MB Markdown file | absent from full reads and prompt bytes |
   566	| Relevant document ranked ninth with tied score | cutoff tie escalates |
   567	| Corpus changes after routing | artifact stale; reroute required |
   568	| Manifest claims unread file | fail closed |
   569	| Mechanical log contains undeclared full read | fail closed |
   570	| Prompt-injection text in document | ignored as instruction; content remains evidence only |
   571	| Proposal exceeds schema budget | proposal rejected and recorded |
   572	| Secret in Story/checklist prose or backticks | value is removed before every host request; deterministic local routing remains available |
   573	| Secret in seed provenance, `sourceRef`, path/title, config, or error metadata | value is hashed or omitted from host-bound and persisted artifacts; the raw mapping stays local only |
   574	| Sanitizer cannot classify a value confidently | host call is skipped and recorded; deterministic local routing continues |
   575	| Host returns secret-like material | proposal is rejected, not persisted, and cannot influence candidate ranking |

   577	## 21. Rollout
   578	
   579	### Shadow
   580	
   581	Target/historical rollout design: run the router beside current bounded reviewer behavior, record candidates, misses, bytes, latency, and what the reviewer actually read, without making candidate evidence mandatory merely because mode is `shadow`.
   582	
   583	Current implemented semantics: when no candidate artifact digest/read binding is supplied, `shadow` remains non-authoritative and the gate does not require one. When a caller does supply `candidateSpecSetDigest`/read binding—as current dispatch examples do—the scope/review handlers validate its signature, freshness, manifest coverage, and escalation resolution fail closed even in `shadow`. Runtime metric/window collection described by the target design is still future work.
   584	
   585	### Warn
   586	
   587	Surface stale/malformed artifacts, budget overruns, read mismatches, and unjustified full scans. Existing signed scope evidence remains authoritative.
   588	
   589	### Enforce
   590	
   591	Require current candidate and read-evidence artifacts for configured lanes. Enforce only after golden recall, finding equivalence, and host failure-path tests pass.
   592	
   593	### Rollback
   594	
   595	Configuration disables candidate enforcement and returns reviewers to explicit tool-driven search with recorded escalation. Rollback must never restore `_reviewPrompt` corpus embedding.

     9	## 0. Current state (code-verified, CLI-only, no server)
    10	
    11	The Authority Python server is deprecated; the system is CLI-only (the CLI signs receipts and
    12	verifies them offline). Verified against the current CLI:
    13	
    14	- **Built and working:** local Ed25519 signing + offline verify (`receipt-bundle.ts`
    15	  `buildReceiptBundle` / `verifyReceiptBundleOffline`; `authority-signing.ts` sign/verify canonical);
    16	  a pure quorum evaluator (`decision-doc-quorum.ts` 3-round × 2-host, strict `materialDigest`;
    17	  `verdicts.ts` `summarizeVerdicts` union-find, fail-closed; `quorum-submit.ts` handler);
    18	  host-B collection via `cross_host_review`, which submits/resumes a ManagedHostRun and records
    19	  host-B `managedRunId`/`managedReceiptId` (`registry.ts` `createCrossHostReviewHandlers`;
    20	  `handlers/cross-host-review.ts`).
    21	- **The three gaps (why Tier-C is not closed):**
    22	  1. **Provenance:** the `HostVerdict` record has NO required signature (`verdicts.ts`; a carried
    23	     `receiptId` is explicitly "not a verified signature"). A verdict proves tree integrity
    24	     (materialHash) but NOT that it came from a specific host's key.
    25	  2. **Independence is a label, not crypto:** `quorum-submit.ts` derives host/session/key from
    26	     string templates and only rejects string collisions. Two "independent" hosts in one store is a
    27	     naming convention, not two signed attestations.
    28	  3. **Same-operator / crypto-deferred boundary:** collection is implemented, but it does not
    29	     earn cryptographic independence. `cross_host_review` auto-drives host B (Codex) on the same
    30	     operator machine and records `managedRunId`/`managedReceiptId`; the collected host-B verdict
    31	     still has no required `HostVerdict` signature (gap 1) and host identity remains a naming
    32	     convention (gap 2). `dispatch_auto` still picks ONE host and is not the collection path.
    33	     Signed-verdict pinning stays deferred (M-crypto / M2).
    34	- **Not covered by pre-reg:** the locked `lattice-experiment-protocol.md` has H1/H2/H3 only; a
    35	  cross-host quorum-formation hypothesis (H4) must be added by amendment.
    36	- **Autopilot:** checkpoint/resume + 429/network health-aware pause/resume are production;
    37	  adaptive-throttle + process-pool parallelism are gated — needed only for the powered campaign
    38	  (Tier-C milestone M4 below), and the proven `experiments/recovery-runner/powered/` scaffolding can
    39	  substitute. (Autopilot's own internal milestones are named by capability here to avoid colliding
    40	  with this plan's M0–M5.)
    41	
    42	## 1. What this closes and what it proves
    43	
    44	Today all evidence (Tier-A engine contract, Tier-B powered ablation) is produced on one operator's
    45	machine — a skeptic must trust the operator. Tier-C makes two **independent vendor hosts**
    46	(Claude + Codex) each emit a **cryptographically signed** verdict on the same code, such that any
    47	third party can **offline-verify** both signatures and their binding to that exact code. It moves
    48	trust from "trust the operator" to "trust the math + two independent vendors." This is the strongest
    49	form of the thesis and the sole gap the paper names for Tier-C.
    50	
    51	## 2. Milestones
    52	
    53	Cheap proof-of-mechanism = M0–M3 (days each, ~zero research risk). Expensive strong claim = M4
    54	(the powered run, real spend). Paper flip = M5. Decision (2026-07-02): do M0–M3 first; M4 only when
    55	a strong external claim is actually needed.
    56	
    57	### M0 — Threat model + key-management decision doc  [doc · small · high-leverage]
    58	Objective: define, before any run, what makes the quorum sound.
    59	- How host A trusts host B's signing public key (a pinned `[hostId → publicKey]` manifest; out-of-band).
    60	- The **independence definition** and its honest boundary: cross-vendor (different companies/models)
    61	  vs. same-operator orchestration — the paper may only claim what the setup earns.
    62	- Replay / stale-materialHash / supersession defenses; key rotation/revocation.
    63	Deliverable: `docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md`.
    64	Acceptance: names the trust anchor, the independence claim + its ceiling, and every fail-closed rule.
    65	Repro-first: exempt (documentation, not material code).
    66	
    67	### M1 — Automatic cross-host review + disagreement surfacing (crypto-deferred)  [build · medium · the mechanism crux]
    68	Decision (2026-07-03): M1 is **crypto-deferred**. On the current single-machine, same-operator
    69	setup, tamper-proofing (signed verdicts / pinned keys) defends against a non-existent adversary —
    70	the value we can earn today is the **adversarial joint decision**, not a signature. So M1 builds the
    71	collection+decision mechanism now and defers the provenance crypto to M-crypto (below,
    72	external-skeptic-only).
    73	
    74	**Current-state supersession:** the bullets below preserve M1's historical
    75	direct-capture design. Production `cross_host_review` now launches/resumes one
    76	ManagedHostRun, and host-B provenance is the sealed terminal `receiptId` plus
    77	exact `managedRunId`; the old stdoutDigest-only direct capture is retired.
    78	Interrupt/TERM/KILL/reap ownership belongs to that ManagedHostRun supervisor,
    79	not to the cross-host controller or caller.
    80	Objective: turn the manual 2-host quorum into an **automatic** cross-host adversarial review that
    81	records a materialHash-bound host-B verdict through the existing capture path and surfaces where
    82	host A (Claude) and host B (Codex) disagree.
    83	- A new `cross_host_review` command auto-runs Codex as an independent **read-only** reviewer over the
    84	  current materialHash-bound change (stdin-piped `codex exec -s read-only -C <worktree>`; parse ONLY
    85	  the structured JSON verdict, record only a `stdoutDigest` for provenance — never raw stdout).
    86	- Fail-closed: no parseable/schema-valid verdict → `blocked` (`codex_review_no_parseable_verdict`);
    87	  a verdict bound to a different materialHash → `blocked` (`codex_review_material_mismatch`).
    88	- Capture the host-B verdict via the existing `submitLocalVerdict` path (binds `materialDigest`,
    89	  appends a `host_verdict` event) with a distinct derived hostId/session/key so the two hosts do not
    90	  collapse in `groupByIndependentHost`.
    91	- `diffFindings` + `jointDecision` (pure): the joint decision is `pass` IFF both hosts pass AND there
    92	  is no finding-level divergence; otherwise `blocked`, surfacing WHICH finding one host raised and the
    93	  other missed (the gap `summarizeVerdicts` does not fill — it only counts pass/fail hosts).
    94	- Dispatch policy gains a NARROW `allowReviewOnlyRealHostSubprocess` flag that permits ONLY a
    95	  read-only Codex reviewer; the general `allowRealHostSubprocess` implementation path for codex, and
    96	  gemini/antigravity, stay refused.
    97	Files: `core/codex-review-leaf.ts` (new), `core/cross-host-review.ts` (new),
    98	`handlers/cross-host-review.ts` (new), `core/dispatch-policy.ts`, `cli/command-catalog.ts`,
    99	`registry.ts`. Crypto files (`receipt-bundle.ts`/`authority-signing.ts`) are explicitly **untouched**.
   100	Acceptance: with an injected fake Codex seam, a `fail` verdict carrying a host-B-only finding yields
   101	`jointDecision === 'blocked'` with `disagreement.onlyHostB.length === 1`; an agreeing case (both pass,
   102	identical findings) yields `jointDecision === 'pass'`, `hasDisagreement === false`; both fail-closed
   103	paths return a synthesized `blocked` verdict and never surface raw stdout.
   104	Repro-first RED: `registry.get('cross_host_review')` FAILS on the pre-fix baseline. SPIKE (done):
   105	codex 0.141.0 emits the verdict JSON cleanly only via the stdin-pipe read-only mechanism (prompt-as-arg
   106	hangs; there is no `--prompt-file`).
   107	
   108	### M-crypto — Provenance: signed verdict + public-key pinning  [build · medium · external-skeptic-only, DEFERRED]
   109	Deferred (2026-07-03): only worth building when a strong EXTERNAL-skeptic claim is actually needed
   110	(pairs with M4's powered campaign). On the current same-operator setup it defends against no present
   111	adversary, so it is explicitly moved out of the near-term M0–M3 block.
   112	Objective: make each verdict cryptographically bound to a distinct pinned host key.
   113	- Each host emits a `receipt-bundle`-signed verdict; bind the signature INTO the `HostVerdict` record.
   114	- Add the pinned `[hostId → publicKey]` manifest.
   115	- Upgrade `summarizeVerdicts` independence from label-distinct to signature-distinct (verify two
   116	  different pinned keys).
   117	Files: `verdicts.ts`, `receipt-bundle.ts`/`authority-signing.ts`, new manifest.
   118	Acceptance: a quorum is valid only if it carries two verdicts signed by two different pinned keys
   119	over the same materialHash; a hard-recompute/full-verify fallback keeps admissibility un-relaxed.

   123	### M2 — Collection: cross-host dispatch-verify verb + handshake  [build · medium]
   124	Current-state note: unsigned host-B collection via `cross_host_review` + ManagedHostRun is
   125	already implemented (section 0). M2 is the remaining signed `dispatch_verify` handshake, not a
   126	claim that host B cannot be auto-driven.
   127	Objective: actually collect host B's signed verdict, no server.

   133	materialHash as host A's; freshness check passes for both.

   135	handshake blocks submission until both hosts are on the same tree sha.
